messages.author: 32586550f710f25b
messages.subject: tuning of poppr::ia
parts:
In order to customise the output plot of the ia() function I would like to customise this function. However, I do not find "where" the functions within ia(), such as should_poppr_be_quiet(), .Ia.Rd()or  poppr.plot()are. Or in other words, how to have them in the global environment of my R session, rather than just within the ia() function. I tried to rewrite the function ia() in order to output me the samp object which is, as far as I can tell, the data for the poppr.plot() function. I guess within this fuction is a ggplot part.

How can I modify the original ia() fuction and save it as my.custom.ia fuction that allows me either to control the graphical parameters or to give me the resampling data that I can feed "manually" into ggplot2?

(I am aware that this is a basic R question, but I still hop that I can get some help in this group).

Best,
L.

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] tuning of poppr::ia
parts:
Hi,

Those are functions that are internal to poppr and not for use outside of it. That being said, ia already returns the data frame of the sampled data by using the valuereturn = TRUE argument: https://grunwaldlab.github.io/poppr/reference/ia.html#if-there-is-sampling-and-valureturn-true

You can use the raw data from that to customize the plot in any way you see fit. You can define a custom plot function to plot this data from there.

Best,

Zhian
